newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: No change to RBNZ's policy implementation - Brash.
newsitem.headline: No change to RBNZ's policy implementation - Brash.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash said on Thursday the bank would make no substantive changes to the way it implements monetary policy.
Possible changes had been canvassed in a consultative paper released in March.

"After reviewing the submissions and in the light of consultations, the Bank has at this stage decided not to proceed with the proposals contained in the consultative paper," Brash said in a statement.
Nevertheless, there had been widespread opposition to the planned change from within the financial community whose views the RBNZ canvassed in detail over the past months.

What had initially been described as an early May deadline for an announcement of decision on whether or not to change had slipped by about a month, and meetings were still being held with market economists as recently as two weeks ago.

In tandem with today's announcement that there will be no change, the bank also said it would revise the way that it presents parts of its forthcoming Monetary Policy Statement on June 27 and similar statements thereafter.

While it explained that the change would not inherently provide new information about its judgement of the extent of inflation pressures, "It simply makes the potential implications for future monetary conditions more explicit," the BNZ said.
